verses.text: Yahweh says to me, “Go, and buy yourself a linen belt, and put it on your waist, and don’t put it in water.”
So I bought a belt according to Yahweh’s word, and put it on my waist.
Yahweh’s word came to me the second time, saying,
“Take the belt that you have bought, which is on your waist, and arise, go to the Euphrates, and hide it there in a cleft of the rock.”
So I went, and hid it by the Euphrates, as Yahweh commanded me.
After many days, Yahweh said to me, “Arise, go to the Euphrates, and take the belt from there, which I commanded you to hide there.”
Then I went to the Euphrates, and dug, and took the belt from the place where I had hidden it; and behold, the belt was ruined. It was profitable for nothing.
Then Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,
“Yahweh says, ‘In this way I, will ruin the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem.

This evil people, who refuse to hear my words, who walk in the stubbornness of their heart, and are gone after other gods to serve them, and to worship them, shall even be as this belt, which is profitable for nothing.

For as the belt clings to the waist of a man, so I have caused to cling to me the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah,’ says Yahweh; ‘that they may be to me for a people, and for a name, and for a praise, and for a glory: but they would not hear.’

“Therefore you shall speak to them this word: ‘Yahweh, the God of Israel says, “Every bottle shall be filled with wine.”’ They will tell you, ‘Do we not certainly know that every bottle shall be filled with wine?’

Then tell them, ‘Yahweh says, “Behold, I will fill all the inhabitants of this land, even the kings who sit on David’s throne, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, with drunkenness.
I will dash them one against another, even the fathers and the sons together,” says Yahweh: “I will not pity, nor spare, nor have compassion, that I should not destroy them.”’”
Hear, and give ear. Don’t be proud; for Yahweh has spoken.

Give glory to Yahweh your God, before he causes darkness, and before your feet stumble on the dark mountains, and, while you look for light, he turns it into the shadow of death, and makes it gross darkness.
But if you will not hear it, my soul shall weep in secret for your pride; and my eye shall weep bitterly, and run down with tears, because Yahweh’s flock is taken captive.
Say to the king and to the queen mother, “Humble yourselves, sit down; for your headdresses have come down, even the crown of your glory.
The cities of the South are shut up, and there is no one to open them. Judah is carried away captive, all of it; it is wholly carried away captive.
Lift up your eyes, and see those who come from the north. where is the flock that was given you, your beautiful flock?
What will you say, when he shall set over you as head those whom you have yourself taught to be friends to you? Shall not sorrows take hold of you, as of a woman in travail?
If you say in your heart, “Why are these things come on me?” For the greatness of your iniquity your skirts are uncovered, and your heels suffer violence.
Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots? Then may you also do good, who are accustomed to do evil.
“Therefore I will scatter them, as the stubble that passes away, by the wind of the wilderness.
This is your lot, the portion measured to you from me,” says Yahweh; “because you have forgotten me, and trusted in falsehood.”
Therefore will I also uncover your skirts on your face, and your shame shall appear.

I have seen your abominations, even your adulteries, and your neighing, the lewdness of your prostitution, on the hills in the field. Woe to you, Jerusalem! You will not be made clean; how long shall it yet be?”

footnotes.content: The Lord asks Jeremiah to buy a linen belt and never wash it—an odd, specific command. When God tells us to do something strange, He's usually teaching us something His own people will need to see. Jeremiah didn't argue or delay.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Obedience begins the moment we hear. Jeremiah obeyed simply—he bought the belt and put it on. There's no record of his doubts or questions, just the doing. That kind of faithfulness, before we understand the lesson, is what the Lord is always looking for.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "The word came to me a second time." The Lord speaks again—He's not done with Jeremiah. Every true calling involves multiple words, multiple turns, sometimes long stretches where we're simply waiting to hear what comes next.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Take the belt to the Euphrates and hide it in a rock cleft—a journey of about 500 miles or more. The Lord asks His prophets not just to speak truth but to live it, to spend their bodies and time on it. Symbolic action, rooted in place.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Again, Jeremiah went and hid it as the Lord commanded. No shortcuts, no editing the instructions. Sometimes the Lord's word asks us to do what looks foolish to the watching world, but the point isn't to impress anyone—it's to stay faithful to what we've been told.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "After many days"—time passes. Jeremiah waits. The Lord speaks again and sends him back to retrieve what he hid. In our own walk, the Lord often asks us to wait long periods before revealing the point of what He's asked us to do.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The belt is ruined, rotted, useless. All those months buried by the Euphrates, exposed to moisture and decay. The prophecy is made tangible—Judah will be like this belt, worthless, spoiled by stubborn pride and unfaithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The word comes again, now with the explanation. Jeremiah has done the hard, strange work—the journey, the waiting—and now he hears why. The Lord always explains His signs to those faithful enough to carry them out.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I will ruin the pride of Judah and Jerusalem." Pride—that is the root. The people have become proud of their place, their temple, their status. But pride and unfaithfulness to the Lord go together like rot in cloth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They refuse to hear His words, they walk in the stubborn stubbornness of their own hearts, and they chase other gods. When a people turn away from the Lord this thoroughly, all their strength—all their status, all their glory—becomes nothing but waste.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "As the belt clings to a man's waist, so I have caused to cling to me the whole house of Israel." The Lord bound Himself to them—close as clothing, intimate. They were meant to be His praise and glory, but they would not hear. Even rejection doesn't change how close He wanted to hold them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A proverb about bottles filled with wine—everyone knows it. The people respond with the obvious, the comfortable thing they already know. But the Lord is about to say something they don't expect, using their own familiar words as a doorway.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will fill all inhabitants of this land with drunkenness—kings, priests, prophets, all of Jerusalem. The word 'drunkenness' here means confusion, stumbling, loss of ability to stand. The Lord is saying: judgment will come on every level of society without exception.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will dash them against one another—fathers and sons together—without pity, mercy, or compassion. This is the language of absolute judgment, not as cruelty but as the end of the Lord's patience with a people who have turned away repeatedly. When He speaks of 'no compassion,' it means the time for mercy has closed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hear and give ear. Don't be proud. The Lord has spoken. This is the call to return before it's too late—the simple, urgent plea to listen and let go of pride. A grandparent's voice would say: 'Your stubbornness will cost you everything.'
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Give glory to the Lord your God before He causes darkness and your feet stumble on dark mountains. Before the light turns to shadow and death. This is the last call—repent while light remains, while you can still see the way back to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If you will not hear, my soul weeps in secret for your pride. Jeremiah's own anguish shows through—he has carried these words from the Lord, and now he grieves for a people who won't turn. The prophet's heart breaks for the flock that is about to be taken captive.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Say to the king and queen mother: Humble yourselves, sit down. Your headdresses have come down, your crown of glory is fallen. The highest are brought low—this is what judgment looks like when it comes to those who held power and refused to turn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The cities of the South are shut up—no one to open them. Judah is carried captive, wholly. The prophecy of the ruined belt has come to pass in this word-picture: the kingdom is shuttered, the people dispersed. This is the end the Lord warned them of.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lift up your eyes and see those who come from the north. Where is the flock that was given you, your beautiful flock? The invaders come from the north—Babylon. The shepherds of Judah have lost their flock, and the Lord asks them to witness it with their own eyes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: What will you say when He sets over you those whom you yourself taught to be your friends? Your allies become your rulers, and the pain of it will be like a woman in labor. Betrayal and conquest—the Lord turns their own choices against them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Why are these things coming on me? Because of the greatness of your iniquity, your skirts are uncovered and your heels suffer violence. The people ask 'why?' but the Lord's answer is clear: your own sin has left you naked and vulnerable before your enemies.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots? Then can you also do good, who are accustomed to do evil? The proverb speaks of what is fixed and unchangeable—and the Lord applies it to Judah's habits of sin. They have practiced evil so long it has become their nature.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Therefore I will scatter them as the stubble that passes away by the wind of the wilderness. The people who refused to cling to the Lord will be blown about like chaff—scattered, homeless, torn from their land.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This is your lot, the portion measured to you from me because you have forgotten me and trusted in falsehood. The Lord Himself measures out what they will receive—the consequence of forgetting Him and running after empty things. No one can appeal this judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will uncover your skirts on your face and your shame shall appear. The language speaks of utter humiliation and exposure—what was hidden and protected will be revealed before all the nations. This is what happens when a people turns from the Lord in defiance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I have seen your abominations, adulteries, neighing, lewdness on the hills. The Lord's patience exhausted, His seeing turned to judgment. Readers today hear an echo in every unchecked appetite: the Lord sees what we think is hidden, and a people who will not return to Him faces exposure.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
